settings.title: Settings
settings.epochsHelp: Maximum number of times to loop through the entire training data. One epoch is one time through the data.
settings.mlpFactorHelp: Change the size of the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) in the transformer blocks. A larger MLP can allow the model to remember more patterns but will increase the number of parameters.
settings.headsHelp: Change the number of attention heads in the transformer blocks. More heads can allow the model to focus on different parts of the input simultaneously.
settings.contextHelp: The **number of previous tokens** the model can see to make its predictions.
settings.batchHelp:
The number of samples processed at the same time to average out any problems.

A larger number can also speed up training but will require more memory.
settings.lrHelp:
How fast to tune the parameters with each training step.

Too low and nothing changes, too high and learning becomes unstable.
settings.temperatureHelp:
After making a prediction, the actual token needs to be selected by using the probability. Some randomness is added to increase diversity.

A **higher temperature produces more random outputs** as it is less likely to select the most obvious next token.

help.layerLimits: How many of the last model layers should be trained. Fewer is faster but may not learn as well. The other layers are locked so they cannot change.
help.checkpointing: Using gradient checkpointing reduces memory usage but slows down training because it must recalculate values instead of saving them.
help.mixedPrecision: Reduces training precision from 32-bit to 16-bit to save memory and time. May not always be supported and could reduce model quality.
help.layerDrop: Randomly drops entire layers during training to improve generalization. The model cannot rely on any one layer to make predictions.
help.dropout: Randomly drops individual parameters during training to improve generalization.
help.warmupSteps: Gradually increases the learning rate for the first few steps to avoid instability when starting from random weights.
help.decayEpochs: Reduce the learning rate slowly over the specified number of epochs to improve convergence. Learns fast at the start but then finds smaller improvements as it goes.
help.weightDecay: Adds a penalty to large parameter values to prevent overfitting.
help.gradClipping: Limits the size of gradients to prevent exploding gradients during training. One bad step can ruin the model so this keeps it under control.
help.validationSplit: A portion of the training data is set aside to test how well the model is learning. This validation data is not shown to the model during training so it cannot cheat.
help.saveToOPFS: Use disk storage for tokens instead of memory. Useful for large datasets but could potentially be a privacy concern.

data.help:
## Text Data

A language model **learns patterns** from example text. The more text you provide, the better it can learn. Even tiny models require **at least 30 million (30M) characters**.

Use **plain unstructured text** like essays, novels or articles that do not include a lot of styling or structure.

You can write your own text, upload files or use our dataset library.

checkmodel.title: Build Model
checkmodel.outdated: The model needs to be rebuilt
checkmodel.help:
## Making the Model

Building a model will allocate memory resources and assign random numbers to the parameters.

If you change the architecture or size of the model, it will need to be rebuilt. Rebuilding will **lose any training you have done** because the parameters become random again.
checkmodel.exceedsSizeLimit: The model has too many parameters.

confirm.title: Rebuild Model
confirm.message: Any training of the current model will be lost. Are you sure you want to rebuild the model?

foundation.title: Pre-trained Models
foundation.help:
## Foundation Models

Foundation models are **pre-trained** on a large amount of text data and can be used as a starting point for your own model.

Select a model that is close to what you want and then adjust it with your own data.

Using a pre-trained model saves time and energy because it has already learned general patterns in language that can be reused.

model.title: Model
model.parametersHelp:
The **total number of numeric parameters** in the model.

More parameters allow the model to learn more patterns but will require more memory, time and data to train.
model.help:
## Your model

This box represents the model you are creating.

A model is a **mathematical representation** of the patterns in your data. It is made up of **numeric parameters** that are adjusted during training to learn those patterns.

Parameters are inputs to equations that predict the next piece in a sequence of text (for example, a word or letter).
model.visualHelp: This diagram shows the structure, or architecture, of your model. There are inputs, multiple layers of parameters and an output. You can edit the shape of the model to change the number of parameters and where they are placed.
model.archHelp:
## Model Architecture

Your model **stores the parameters** that are adjusted during training and used to predict the next token.

The architecture of the model determines how many parameters it has and how they are arranged. Changing where the parameters are located will influence the kinds of patterns it can learn.

training.help:
## Model Training

The learning process where the **parameters are slowly adjusted** up or down until it can reproduce the patterns found in your example data.

You can click the circular progress indicator to switch between power and time. Time (or power) remaining is how long it will take to look at all of your data.
training.attentionHelp: A short example taken from your data. The model is trying to predict the highlighted token based on the previous text. The example is converted to numeric tokens. Each layer of the model pays attention to different parts of the text.
training.modelBoxHelp: Each layer of your model contributes towards the final prediction, one layer at a time. The parameters inside each layer are tuned by how well they contributed or not.
training.lossBoxHelp: After the model has made its prediction it is scored against the correct answer. Loss is a measure of how wrong the model's prediction was, so the training process tries to reduce this number.

generator.help:
## Generating Text

After training the model parameters, they can be used to predict the next token (**"inference"**) in a sequence of text by using your prompt and any previous predictions (called **context**). This sequential process is known as **autoregressive generation**.

How well your model generates or responds to prompts depends on how well it was trained and the quality of the data.

training.title: Training Monitor
training.validationHelp:
## Validation Data

Some of your data is used to test how well the model is learning instead of memorising.

This validation data is not shown to the model during training so it cannot cheat.
training.accuracyHelp: **Accuracy** is the percentage of predictions that were correct.
training.lossHelp: **Loss** is a measure of how wrong the model's predictions were. It refers to the loss of information.

tools.dataHelp: Your tokenised training data provides a source of examples when training. It is not available to the model when generating text after training.

tokeniser.invalidWarning: The vocabulary was not selected from the current data.
tokeniser.trainedWarning: The model is already trained, changing the vocabulary may cause problems.
tokeniser.includeSpecialHelp: Special tokens are control tokens that help structure the text and output.
tokeniser.help:
## Token Vocabulary

The vocabulary is a set of letters, words or parts of words that are the building blocks of language for the model. These building blocks are called **tokens** and are each **assigned a unique number**.

Building a vocabulary involves processing your data to find the most common tokens in the text. Since the size of the vocabulary is limited, it is important to choose the best common tokens.

errors.too_small_vocab: The vocabulary size is too small for the data.

tokeniseData.title: Tokenise Data
tokeniseData.tooManyTokens: You have more tokens than needed
tokeniseData.help:
## Tokenising

Your text data needs to be split into the numeric tokens that the mathematical model can work with.

A progress bar indicates how many tokens have been generated from your data. **Larger models need more tokens** so the progress bar shows how many you may need to train it well.
